title: Improved bounds on stabilizer extent and Clifford rank
abstract: We prove that every pure state of stabilizer rank at most $k$ has stabilizer extent at most $2^{O(\sqrt{k\log(k+1)})}$, and establish the analogous bound for the squared Clifford coefficient norm of Clifford-rank-$k$ operators. This implies stabilizer fidelity at least $2^{-O(\sqrt{k\log(k+1)})}$, resolving the quantitative conjecture of (Mehraban-Tamasbi, STOC, 2025), and proves an $Ω(n^2/\log n)$ lower bound for the approximate stabilizer rank of tensor powers of any non-stabilizer qubit state. The latter result generalizes the best-known lower bound for tensor powers of $T$-states (Mehraban-Tamasbi, STOC, 2024) to arbitrary non-stabilizer qubit states, including magic states.   As a consequence of the Clifford rank--norm inequality, we obtain an $Ω(n^2/\log n)$ lower bound for exact representations of $n$-bit AND function by quadratic phases, improving the previous best-known linear bound. Further consequences rule out pseudorandom state and unitary ensembles with approximate stabilizer and Clifford rank $O((\log n)^2/\log\log n)$, respectively, a $\log n$ improvement over prior work (Kalra-Sinha, Quantum, 2026). We also obtain tomography algorithms for states of stabilizer rank at most $k$, with $poly(n)2^{O(\sqrt{k\log(k+1)})}$ time and copy complexity, a nearly square-root improvement in the exponent over the best-known algorithm.
summary: This theoretical paper establishes significantly improved quantitative bounds connecting the stabilizer rank of quantum states and operators to their respective extents and Clifford ranks. By proving these bounds, the authors derive new lower bounds for the complexity of quantum states, such as tensor powers, and provide tighter characterizations of pseudorandom quantum ensembles. This work advances the understanding of resource quantification in quantum information theory.
main_problem: The paper aims to establish improved quantitative bounds relating the stabilizer rank ($\chi$) of quantum states and operators to their respective 'extent' ($\xi$) and Clifford rank ($\chi_C$).
main_result: It proves that for a state of stabilizer rank $k$, its extent is bounded by $2^{O(\sqrt{k\log(k+1)})}$, and derives lower bounds for the approximate stabilizer rank of tensor powers of non-stabilizer states.
method: The authors use techniques involving decomposing states into stabilizer components, applying randomized projections, and relating operator bounds to state bounds via the Choi map formalism.
model_or_system: The focus is on quantum states and operators acting on $n$ qubits, specifically analyzing the structure and complexity of stabilizer states and general non-stabilizer states.
key_observables: Stabilizer Rank ($\chi$), Stabilizer Extent ($\xi$), Clifford Rank ($\chi_C$), and Stabilizer Fidelity ($F_S$).
important_parameters: The rank $k$ (the maximum allowed stabilizer rank) and the number of qubits $n$.
main_assumptions: The analysis relies on the ability to decompose states into sums of stabilizer states and the use of specific projection techniques to control the coefficients.
paper_structure: The paper builds from establishing the core quantitative bounds (Theorem 1.1 and 1.2) relating rank to extent/norm, which are then leveraged to prove lower bounds for state complexity (tensor powers, AND function) and characterize pseudorandomness.
why_interesting: The derived bounds provide concrete, improved quantitative measures of quantum state complexity, which are crucial for understanding the limits of quantum computation and simulation.
